claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start by getting the first question for the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To start the assessment, I need to understand the age of the child or children you're claiming for.

**How old is the child you're inquiring about?**

Please let me know:
- The child's age (or approximate age)
- If you have multiple children, please provide the ages for each one

The key information I need is whether they are:
- Under 16 years old
- Between 16-19 years old
- 20 years old or over

Once you provide this information, I can guide you through the rest of the eligibility check!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 18 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that context! So you're looking to claim Child Benefit for your son **Alex, who is 18 years old** and lives at home with you.

Since Alex is 18, he falls into the **16-19 age category**. For this age group, I need to check whether he's in full-time education or training to determine eligibility.

**Could you please tell me: Is Alex currently in full-time education or training?**

This could include:
- Secondary or further education (like A-levels, BTec, etc.)
- University or higher education
- An apprenticeship or other approved training scheme
- Other full-time vocational training

Please let me know his current status so I can proceed with the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment. He finished school and went straight into work - he's got a full-time job at the local supermarket.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 18 and working full-time (not in education or training), I need to check one more important thing about his work situation.

**Is Alex working 24 hours or more per week in his full-time job at the supermarket?**

This is an important threshold for Child Benefit eligibility for 16-19 year olds who aren't in education or training.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is - it's a full-time job, so he's working well over 24 hours a week.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Based on the information you've provided:

- **Alex is 18 years old**
- **He is not in full-time education or training**
- **He is working 24 hours or more per week** (full-time job at the supermarket)

Unfortunately, this means **Alex does not qualify as a "qualifying child" for Child Benefit purposes**. Under the Child Benefit rules, when a young person aged 16-19 is not in full-time education or training, they must be under 24 hours per week of work to potentially qualify. Since Alex is working full-time (well over 24 hours per week), he falls outside the eligibility criteria.

Let me provide you with the formal outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Outcome: NOT ELIGIBLE**

**Summary:**
- Alex is not eligible for Child Benefit
- The reason is that he is 16-19 years old, not in full-time education or training, and working 24 hours or more per week

**What this means:**
Child Benefit is designed to support families with young people who are dependent on them. Once young people reach 16 and start working full-time, they're typically considered more independent and may no longer qualify.

**Next steps:**
- If Alex's circumstances change (for example, if he were to join a full-time education course or training programme), you could reapply for Child Benefit at that point
- If you have other children under the qualifying age, you may be able to claim Child Benefit for them instead

Is there anything else I can help you with, or do you have any other children you'd like me to check eligibility for?
